metadata.source_title: Evolution and Selection of Quantitative Traits

blocks.content: Recall that in our distinction between long-term and asymptotic response, the former is attributable to the existing variation at the start of selection, while the latter is the expected eventual rate of response due to the input of new mutation. When the effective population size is small, essentially all of the observed response is due to the initial variation, with the population reaching an apparent limit until the appearance of new mutations allows for further response. In larger populations, these two components of response become more difficult to separate, and no limit may be observed when in fact all of the initial variation has been exhausted. Much of the initial theory of long-term response ignored mutation, and we examine this drift-only version first, as it provides a good description of how a population exhausts its initial variation.
